bull.b: CTV is the company’s strongest growth engine, with contribution rising 39% and leading accounts growing in the mid-40% range. This supports Magnite’s positioning in streaming monetization and provides a durable growth runway as programmatic advertising expands across connected-TV inventory.

Rapid EBITDA expansion alongside strong cash generation indicates meaningful operating leverage in Magnite’s platform model. Higher margins and free cash flow can fund product investment, strengthen financial resilience, and improve the company’s ability to capture sustained digital advertising growth.

Expanded partnerships increase Magnite’s access to premium supply and deepen its role in publishers’ advertising infrastructure. Multi-year, primary-platform, and exclusive arrangements can reinforce ecosystem integration, support transaction volume, and make the platform more difficult to displace.

bear.b: Weakness in display and limited growth across the broader DV+ segment could restrain consolidated expansion outside CTV. Although mobile in-app, commerce media, and audio offer opportunities, a largely stagnant segment reduces diversification and may limit leverage from Magnite’s wider platform.

Changes in how users reach online content can reduce the volume or quality of monetizable open-web inventory. If search and referral traffic continue shifting toward answer engines, Magnite may face persistent pressure on auction activity, publisher yield, and growth in non-CTV channels.

Magnite’s agentic advertising tools have not yet translated into substantial transaction dollars, making the opportunity commercially unproven. Continued experimentation without broad adoption could delay revenue benefits and require ongoing investment before the technology meaningfully improves platform growth.
